comparison: Perfect agreement on C6, C32, C40. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the scale of data generation (5378 predicted + 3 crystallographic structures). All reviewers praise this as a 'vast resource' and 'massive undertaking.'
Perfect agreement on C7, C8. Both accept the phylogenetic organization and clade structure without question. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'key insertions define the various Nif groups.'
Perfect agreement on C9, C10. Both support the high pLDDT prediction confidence metrics. Peer reviewers describe analyses as 'convincing' without challenging prediction quality.

Strong agreement on C11-C14, C41-C43. Both support that structural predictions capture phylogenetically meaningful variation. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'structural variations correlate with phylogenetic relationships' and provide 'strong insight.' OpenEval includes C44 which peers address separately in R18.

Perfect agreement on C15, C16, C46-C48, C51-C52. Both support the identification of major structural innovations, particularly the K-subunit N-terminus evolution. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'key insertions define the various Nif groups.'
Strong agreement on C17, C54, C55. Both support structural characteristics of insertions. Peer review also includes C18, C53 (additive evolution pattern) which OpenEval addresses separately in R8.

Perfect agreement on C49, C50. Both support the ecological correlations linking structural features to host oxygen tolerance. Peer reviewers note 'strong insight into how structural evolution correlates with environmental and biological phenotypes.'

Agreement on C18, C53 regarding additive evolution pattern. OpenEval treats this as separate finding; peer reviewers group with insertion characteristics (R6). Both accept the observation without critique.

Perfect agreement on C19-C21, C59-C61. Both support clade-specific structural attributes and computational analyses of surface area, contacts, and binding affinities. Described as 'convincing' by peer reviewers.
Perfect agreement on C22. Both support the correlation finding, though OpenEval notes weak correlation and unclear biological significance. Peer reviewers accept without specific discussion.

Agreement on C62, C63 regarding early structural innovations. OpenEval treats as synthesis of structural analysis; peer reviewers group with broader evolutionary conclusions (C33, C38) about conservation and innovation being central findings.

Perfect agreement on C23-C25, C64-C65. Both support the experimental targets and age estimates for ancestral crystallography. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge examination of 'three ancestral nitrogenase variants.'
Perfect agreement on C26, C27. Both support crystallographic observations about differences in crystallization conditions. Accepted as part of 'valuable study' without concerns.

Strong agreement on C69-C73, C75-C76 regarding crystallographic details. OpenEval also includes C28-C30, C74 which peer reviewers address in R12. Both support structural characterization as 'convincing.'

Agreement on C28-C30, C74 regarding RMSD measurements and structural similarity. Peer reviewers accept these as part of convincing data analyses; OpenEval groups with broader crystallographic results (R14).

Critical difference in evaluation type. OpenEval rates C77-C82 as UNCERTAIN, noting functional interpretations are speculative and not experimentally validated. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting substitution analysis and mechanistic hypotheses as part of 'convincing' analyses without raising concerns about speculation.

Perfect agreement on C31, C83. Both support validation of predictions against experimental structures. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by describing analyses as 'convincing' and providing 'unique insights.'

Agreement on C33 (conservation of core features) and synthesis of major findings. OpenEval also includes C85-C86; peer reviewers group C33 with broader evolutionary conclusions (C38, C62-C63) about dual finding of conservation and innovation.

Agreement on C85, C86 regarding phylogenetic signal and early insertion events. Both support these as major findings, with peer reviewers noting 'strong insight' into structural-environmental correlations.

Critical difference in evaluation type. OpenEval rates C34, C36-C37, C56, C58 as UNCERTAIN, noting functional mechanisms are speculative and require experimental validation despite solid structural observations. Peer reviewers rate C36-C37, C56 as SUPPORTED, accepting mechanistic hypotheses without challenging speculation. Timing/context (C34) accepted by both.

Partial overlap on C34. OpenEval groups timing/ecological context with speculative mechanisms (UNCERTAIN overall). Peer reviewers treat evolutionary-environmental correlation (C34, C85-C86) as key SUPPORTED finding providing 'strong insight.'

Critical difference in evaluation type. OpenEval rates C57-C58 as UNCERTAIN, noting functional capability (C58) is inferred without direct experimental evidence or bound structure predictions. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting structural inference as part of overall insertion analysis without raising concerns about lack of experimental validation.

Agreement on C38-C39, C95 as overarching conclusions. Both support the alignment with environmental transitions and evolutionary interpretations. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'strong insight into how structural evolution correlates with environmental and biological phenotypes.' OpenEval notes causal connection involves inference beyond direct data but still rates SUPPORTED.
Partial overlap on C38. OpenEval groups as overarching conclusion with C39, C95. Peer reviewers group C38 with C33, C62-C63 as central finding about conservation and innovation.

Perfect agreement on C66, C67. Both support these claims citing prior functional characterization work. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge 'reduced activity in Azotobacter vinelandii' from earlier studies.

Agreement on C84 regarding distribution of ancestral substitutions. OpenEval treats as context for interface substitutions; peer reviewers group with C77-C82 substitution analysis. Both accept observation.

Agreement on C45 regarding AlphaFold2 limitations with metal cofactors. OpenEval groups with C93-C94 (future improvements); peer reviewers group with C44 (active site conservation). Both accept limitation without concern.

Agreement on C93, C94 regarding methodology limitations and future improvements. Both accept these as appropriate acknowledgments of current AlphaFold2 capabilities. Peer reviewers' positive assessment indicates acceptance of methodological scope.

Perfect agreement on C91, C92. Both support these caveats and alternative evolutionary frameworks. OpenEval and peer reviewers both accept nuanced discussion of uncertainty about adaptive significance.

OpenEval explicitly evaluates background claims C1-C5, C35, C87-C90 as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background/context claims, focusing instead on novel findings and interpretations.
